subject: Marketplace rate-card reconciliation plan + next steps
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya@acme-retail.com>, John Lee <john.lee@amazon.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-22T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Marketplace rate-card reconciliation plan + next steps

Thanks again for the time today — good to surface where the two tracks intersect (Acme's internal PPU targets vs. marketplace private-offer constraints). Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get to a private-offer draft that matches your procurement cadence.

Recap (from our call)
- Target monthly tokens: baseline 200M tokens; expected peak 1.2B tokens during holiday promo windows.
- Acme preferred commercial target: $800 - $1,200 per 1M tokens for the core model (chat/generation).
- Current constraint: AWS private-offer minimum unit is typically expressed as a USD/month commitment across SKUs; we need to translate to $/1M tokens to compare to Acme's internal forecasts.

What I attached
- rdw_acme_rate_matrix_v1.csv — draft mapping (rows: AWS/GCP/Azure SKU -> inferred $/1M tokens using our tokenization profile).
- mutual_action_plan_acme.pdf — suggested milestones for PO, SOC evidence, and Marketplace listing.

Proposed immediate next steps
1) Priya: confirm the 200M / 1.2B token ranges and whether the $/1M target is firm or a top-of-funnel ask (i.e., is $800 your negotiating floor or target).
2) John (AWS): can you validate whether the sample SKU mapping in rdw_acme_rate_matrix_v1.csv aligns with how AWS will express reserved capacity vs. private-offer unit rates? If AWS needs a single committed $ amount rather than a unit price, we can show the equivalent USD commitment per month for the three bands.
3) Marissa/Ben (internal): refine the matrix with the production tokenization profile (attached) and include two quantized model options (fp16/full) so procurement can see tradeoffs.
4) Schedule: propose a short sync next Tue to review revised matrix and draft private-offer language — link: https://cal.com/tessa/rate-card-sync

Ask: Priya, could you share Acme's preferred signature (PO) timeline and any minimum contract term constraints? That will affect whether we recommend a multi-month commit or a tiered burst model.

Thanks — staying flexible on structure, want to make sure unit economics map cleanly across provider offers.

—
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Email: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 415-555-0134

Attachment: rdw_acme_rate_matrix_v1.csv (CSV, 42KB), mutual_action_plan_acme.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

From: Priya Shah <priya@acme-retail.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: John Lee <john.lee@amazon.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T17:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace rate-card reconciliation plan + next steps

Thanks Tessa — helpful summary. A couple quick clarifications from Acme side:

- Token bands: baseline 180–220M / month; expected burst up to 1.1–1.3B during Black Friday/Cyber. So your 200M/1.2B is fine as a planning midpoint.
- Budget posture: procurement has given us a target of ~$900 / 1M tokens as the internal benchmark for negotiations (that is the number our finance team wants to see net of marketplace fees). That is not an absolute floor, but it is the number we want to validate against the private-offer math.
- Term: Acme prefers 12-month committed terms for discounts, but procurement is open to 6-month pilot for first 3 months with a backfill/true-up for the remainder.

I attached our internal forecast (Acme_forecast_Q3_Q4.xlsx) with the monthly token curve; please use it to calculate $/1M at each commitment tier. Also cc'd Luis from our cloud partner team — he'll help coordinate on cross-cloud recommendations (we are evaluating multi-cloud footprint).

Next: if AWS can express the private-offer as a committed $ per month + per-token overage rate, that would be easiest to map to our finance model.

—
Priya Shah
Director, AI Platform | Acme Retail
priya@acme-retail.com

Attachment: Acme_forecast_Q3_Q4.xlsx (XLSX, 88KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya@acme-retail.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, John Lee <john.lee@amazon.com>
Date: 2027-05-24T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace rate-card reconciliation plan + next steps

Thanks Priya — reviewed your forecast and did a quick reconciliation against the draft matrix. Key notes:

> On Tue, May 22, 2027 at 2:02 PM Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai> wrote:
> > - Target monthly tokens: baseline 200M tokens; expected peak 1.2B tokens during holiday promo windows.
> > - Acme preferred commercial target: $800 - $1,200 per 1M tokens for the core model (chat/generation).

Internal reconciliation summary (quick math)
- Using Acme_forecast_Q3_Q4 and our production tokenization profile, the effective token mix yields ~1.8 tokens/word for chat (we used that to normalize across models).
- Mapping approach: we computed an implied $/1M for each provider SKU by taking the SKU monthly cost divided by modeled monthly tokens under three commitment bands (Pilot: 200M, Commit: 500M, Enterprise: 1.2B). See attached updated CSV: rdw_acme_rate_matrix_v1.csv (I updated the Commit/Enterprise rows).
- Two recommended visible options for procurement:
  1) Committed $/month with aggressive tiered discount (favored if Acme will sign 12 months). We show equivalence to $/1M to make ranking apples-to-apples.
  2) 6-month pilot with a true-up clause — express as a smaller committed $/month + capped overage rate per 1M tokens. Helps mitigate initial risk.

Open questions for AWS (John)
- Does AWS allow listing private-offers with explicit per-token equivalence in the offer metadata, or do you prefer a single USD commitment and a descriptive equivalence?
- If AWS requires a USD commitment only, we'll produce a conversion table that shows the equivalent $/1M for each SKU and recommend the commitment band that aligns with Acme's $900 target.

Next steps (internal owners)
- Ben: can you run a quick sensitivity table on the matrix that shows net $/1M after estimated marketplace fees (AWS Marketplace fee + Redmwood recommended fee) so Acme can see net to vendor vs. gross?
- Tessa: once John confirms format, we'll iterate private-offer draft and circulate to Priya + procurement for review.

Thanks — attaching updated CSV.

—
Marissa Cole
Head of Channel Partnerships | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachment: rdw_acme_rate_matrix_v1.csv (updated, CSV, 47KB)

From: John Lee <john.lee@amazon.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@acme-retail.com>, Luis Romero <luis@cloudpartnerventures.com>
Date: 2027-05-25T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace rate-card reconciliation plan + next steps

Appreciate the clear matrix. Quick answers from the AWS side:

- Format: AWS private-offers are captured as committed USD amounts tied to product SKUs; the marketplace UI doesn't have a native $/1M token field. That said, including a conversion table in the offer documentation (and in the private-offer attachment) is standard practice and acceptable. We can also include a ‘billing note’ that shows the equivalence so Acme's finance can map.
- Mechanics: you can structure as (a) fixed monthly commitment across chosen SKUs + (b) overage price per unit. The private-offer will enforce the commitment and attribute usage to the SKU.
- Recommendation: for Acme's profile, propose the following mapping (we'll validate on our side when the SKU list is final):
  * Pilot band (200M tokens): commit $90,000/month -> implied ~$450 / 1M tokens (this gets you strong entry pricing but is a higher relative spend).
  * Mid band (500M tokens): commit $320,000/month -> implied ~$640 / 1M tokens.
  * Enterprise band (1.2B tokens): commit $720,000/month -> implied ~$600 / 1M tokens.

These numbers are illustrative — they assume the SKU mix in rdw_acme_rate_matrix_v1.csv and typical marketplace fee structure. If Acme's target is ~$900/1M net, the mid/enterprise band numbers can be adjusted by changing SKU allocation or committing a longer term.

Next: I'll ask Marketplace Ops to review a draft private-offer if you send the SKU list and the preferred commit band. Happy to join the sync on Tue.

—
John Lee
Marketplace Partner Manager, AWS
john.lee@amazon.com
Phone: +1 206-555-0128
